A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DepthSplat with the same authors and central methodology. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original depth-estimation and Gaussian-splatting experiments, including component ablations, benchmark comparisons, and cross-task pre-training results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds cross-dataset rendering comparisons, pre-training controls, efficiency measurements, and qualitative results in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The multi-view cost volumes, monocular feature branch, feature fusion, hierarchical depth regression, Gaussian prediction, and training objectives remain substantively unchanged. Section 3.4 newly identifies the Gaussian head as a 2D U-Net receiving image, depth, and feature information; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The named datasets and depth/view-synthesis tasks are retained. V2 adds direct RealEstate10K-to-DL3DV rendering generalization under small and large camera baselines (Table 7), extending evaluation to a distinct domain-shift scenario. V1 already mentions reconstruction with 6 and 12 input views, so those view counts are not entirely new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds TranSplat, reporting 26.69 PSNR, 0.875 SSIM, and 0.125 LPIPS. Table 3 removes the Depth Anything-only initialization comparator from that depth experiment, although it remains in the separate rendering-transfer experiment, now Table B.1. V1's standalone qualitative comparison with UniMatch in Figure 5 is also removed; the ScanNet quantitative comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation design with pre-training/fine-tuning combinations in Table 3, direct cross-dataset rendering tests separated by camera baseline, and two-view timing/memory measurements at 256×256 and 512×512 in Appendix A. Table 3 also describes the retained UniMatch + Depth Anything score row as training from random initialization. This revises the reported initialization setting but leaves its actual meaning ambiguous and does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine depth before supervised fine-tuning (Table 3), rendering robustness under dataset shift (Table 7 and Figure C.2), and resource scaling across model sizes and resolutions (Table A.1). Figure C.1 adds depth/error comparisons isolating pre-training, while Figure 6 and Figures C.4–C.5 add generalization examples. V1's UniMatch depth case and varying-view appendix montage are removed or replaced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The retained validation curves in Figure 1 are learning curves, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Table 3's two conditions without fine-tuning, TranSplat scores, cross-dataset rendering scores, efficiency measurements, and qualitative examples. New Table 7 reports DepthSplat/MVSplat PSNR of 20.29/19.19 for small baselines and 17.50/16.26 for large baselines. The mono-only row in v1 Table 3 and parameter counts for three model variants are omitted. Matched benchmark accuracy scores and the transfer results moved from v1 Table 7 to v2 Table B.1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss functions retain their substance. Equation 1 distributes the same gradient-loss weight across its two terms, with a minor parenthesis typesetting defect. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about mutual benefits between depth estimation and Gaussian splatting, unsupervised pre-training, and benchmark leadership remain unchanged. V2's introduction adds the specific capability claim of reconstruction at 512×960 from up to 12 views, refining v1's existing, less specific large-scene/360-degree reconstruction statement in Section 4.4.

C2.justification: V2 adds a hypothesis that pre-training regularizes learning toward better minima and improves generalization, and interprets larger gains with fewer views as sparse-view robustness. Appendix C.4 explains reported high-resolution memory advantages through lower feature resolution and local attention. The camera-pose requirement remains unchanged, while the monocular-feature discussion more precisely identifies Depth Anything V2 as best for view synthesis.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents the high-resolution recipe: the small model, 448×768 training, 200K iterations each on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, batch size 8, and 2–6 training views. V2 also specifies Gaussian-head inputs, A100 efficiency measurements, and TartanAir initialization for Table B.1. Conversely, it omits v1's 5% warm-up, explicit RealEstate10K split correspondence, and exact DL3DV training-scene count. These omissions do not establish changed experiments; the project and code links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused positioning against Flash3D and TranSplat, emphasizing multiple-view reconstruction and early feature fusion, and cites Erhan et al. for the pre-training interpretation. It also supplies references for previously listed baselines and drops the MVS2D citation. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most methodological prose are retained. Local revisions move fusion-related positioning into the introduction, shorten background passages, clarify terminology, and rewrite experimental explanations. The appendix is reorganized from A.1–A.2 into sections A–D, largely to accommodate added material.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Table 3 is restructured, Table 1's parameter column is partly relocated to Table A.1, and v1 Table 7 becomes Table B.1. New generalization and efficiency tables, an expanded RealEstate10K figure, and added or replaced main-text and appendix panels substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens an already experimentally supported paper through cross-dataset results in Table 7, efficiency measurements in Table A.1, and reproducibility details in Appendix D. The main method and benchmark conclusions remain stable. These gains are tempered by Table 3's ambiguous relabeling of an identically scored pre-trained comparator as random initialization and the loss of earlier warm-up and split disclosures, limiting the net quality improvement.
